chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.steer` checks only whether the handle has the `steer` capability and then records the text, so it succeeds even after the fake lane has been stopped or its script is complete. For example, construct `FakeLane(capabilities=("steer",))`, start a handle, call `stop(handle)` (whose `status` then reports `state="stopped"`), and then call `steer(handle, "next")`; the method returns `L.ok("recorded")` and appends `"next"` to `handle.steered`. A real lane cannot be steered after it has exited or been stopped, so tests driving swarm/ETA behaviour through this fake can falsely conclude that post-stop steering worked. The method should also reject steering when `h.stopped` is true or `h.cursor >= len(h.script)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane.steer

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest shows this change adds the new Lane port in `ddflow/adapters/lanes.py` and `ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py`, but it also modifies `ddflow/services/lane_driver.py` to re-export the contract/registry. [r-adapters] says a new port touches only its own files and that external dependencies go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; a service module outside `ddflow/adapters` is not one of the port’s own files. This creates a second public import path for the Lane port in a shared service file, so later changes to that shim can collide with the port implementation and violate the “one place” intent of the rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_driver.py:6

chunk_findings.detail: The new documentation states that the Lane port is `ddflow/adapters/lanes.py` while its default adapter is `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py`. The change’s conformance requires the port Protocol to live in `ddflow/adapters` next to its default adapter and registry, and [r-adapters] requires the external dependency (launching and watching an agent process) to be behind a port in `ddflow/adapters`. As documented, the default implementation of the port is outside the adapters package, so changing or swapping the default adapter touches both the port/registry and a service module rather than one place; if the service module is not imported, `driver_for("process-headless")` can return `unavailable` despite the docs calling it the default adapter. This violates [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/lanes.md:1-4

chunk_findings.detail: The `settle` helper uses wall-clock `time.time()` for its 10-second deadline. If the system clock is stepped forward by more than 10 seconds while the real `ProcessHeadless` conformance test is waiting (e.g. NTP correction, VM/host clock adjustment, or another test that manipulates `time.time`), the loop exits even though `lane.status(h).state` may still be `"running"`; the next assertion then fails with `running` instead of `exited`. A monotonic clock (`time.monotonic()`) or the lane's own timeout would avoid this environment-dependent failure.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_lanes.py:58

chunk_findings.detail: The task states the Lane contract includes `cleanup` (LaunchSpec, observe, steer, cleanup), but `FakeLane` implements only `start`, `events`, `steer`, `stop`, and `status`. A conformance case that runs the same contract cases against the adapter and the fake, or any test that calls `cleanup` on a returned handle, will raise `AttributeError: 'FakeLane' object has no attribute 'cleanup'`, so the fake does not satisfy the port it is registered for.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane

chunk_findings.detail: The new port records its default adapter as `ddflow.services.lane_headless`, an implementation outside `ddflow/adapters`; `driver_for("process-headless")` imports that service module. This violates [r-adapters]: the port/adapter pair is not contained under `ddflow/adapters`, so changing or swapping the default adapter still touches shared `ddflow/services` files rather than only the new port's own files.

chunk_findings.detail: The test suite runs the real `lh.ProcessHeadless()` adapter, which starts a child Python process during tests; the fake `FakeLane` already exists and is used elsewhere, but [r-adapters] states tests should use a fake instead of the network or a subprocess. This can hang or fail in a CI or sandbox environment where launching a subprocess is slow or restricted, so the change violates that guidance.
